800	#### VR7 — linked versions: shapes in the model, the recipe and export (asked)
801	
802	- **What a person gets:** nothing visible yet. A project can hold a 9:16 shape whose framing
803	  follows every edit of the main cut, and Export can write any shape.
804	- **Core:**
805	  - The fields of VR-70, VR-71 and VR-73, behind format N+1 with `schema_vN.rs`.
806	  - `framing.rs` (new): evaluation, reusing `actions.rs`'s curve reading.
807	  - The recipe's placement through F_v (VR-72).
808	  - `RecipeOptions.shape` and the export override `shape` (VR-74).
809	  - The carries (VR-75) in `edit_split.rs`, `edit_clip_timing.rs`, `edit_link.rs`,
810	    `frame_grid.rs`, `time_bounds.rs` and `edit_background.rs`.
811	  - Ops `add_shape`, `set_shape`, `remove_shape`, and `set_framing` (an entry's base) with the
812	    action ops taking an optional `shape`.
813	- **FFI:** `rc_project_frame_recipe_opts`'s options JSON carries `shape` (header :428). No new
814	  export.
815	- **Swift:** `ProjectSnapshot` decodes the fields in a new file after its toll. Export takes
816	  `shape`.
817	- **MCP mirror:** the new op tools; `export`'s `shape`.
818	- **Docs:** spec §5.2, §5.3, §5.4's note, §6c, §7.3, §7.8; §2's note.
819	- **Tolls first** (each a pure move gated alone):
820	  - `model.rs` (570): `Canvas`, `CanvasOutput` and their defaults out to `model_canvas.rs`.
821	  - `ProjectSnapshot.swift` (1454): its named seam, the audio group out to `AudioProps.swift`.
822	  - `recipe.rs` (547): its named seam, the content hash out to `recipe_hash.rs`, if the hook would
823	    pass 590.
824	- **Proof:**
825	  1. A split, a trim, a speed change and a paste each carry framing.
826	  2. A shape's export equals the copy path's export of the same cut frame for frame. Both are made
827	     from the same planner path, so the comparison is byte for byte at sampled frames.
828	  3. An old project opens unchanged.
829	- **Mutants:** one per carry, and the shape option ignored by export.
830	- **Question for the owner (the gate of VR7–VR9):** build linked versions now? *Recommended: yes if
831	  JOB-35's trial shows re-making copies after master edits was a real cost. Otherwise file VR7–VR9
832	  as one issue carrying this design.*
833	
834	#### VR8 — linked versions: preview and canvas editing per shape
835	
836	- **What a person gets:** a Shape popup beside the preview picks the main shape or 9:16. In 9:16 the
837	  canvas handles move the clip's framing, not its placement, and the action lane shows the framing
838	  list.
839	- **Decisions to draft at VR7:**
840	  - VR-80: where the popup lives.
841	  - VR-81: what the inspector's Transform shows in a shape.
842	  - VR-82: what a new clip gets in an existing shape. *Recommended:* the shape's follow, analysed
843	    on demand.
844	  - VR-83: the preview rebuild rule from VR-S4.
845	- **Manual check:** JOB-38, switching and editing per shape.
846	
847	#### VR9 — Make Vertical Version writes a linked shape
848	
849	- **What a person gets:** the sheet's "Make a Copy" becomes a choice of "Add to This Project"
850	  (linked) or "Make a Copy".
851	- **Decisions to draft at VR7:**
852	  - VR-90: the planner writes F into `shapes`, with no composition.
853	  - VR-91: captions and re-laid graphics go on shape-only tracks.
854	  - VR-92: backdrops go on a shape-only track.
855	  - VR-93: `make_vertical_version {link: true}`.
856	- **Proof:** the linked shape's export equals the VR3 copy's frame for frame on the fixture project.
857	
858	### Samples and fixtures
859	
860	**From the owner** (cameras: LUMIX GH5, iPhone 18 Pro). Each is added to `samples/README.md` with
861	what it measures. No phase waits for one; a phase uses the synthetic fixture until it exists.
862	
863	- **VR-A — `talking-head-gh5-4k.mov`.**
864	  - *What:* 3–5 minutes, one take, the owner at a desk on the GH5 at 4K. Natural movement, one
865	    lean out of frame to the side, one stand-up-and-leave of about 3 s, and about 5 s turned away.
866	    The owner writes the times of the leave and the turn.
867	  - *Measures:* VR-S1's rate, size, device and human-rectangle rules; VR-S2's false cuts; VR-S3's
868	    containment and moves per minute; JOB-31.
869	- **VR-B — `talking-head-iphone-applelog.mov`.**
870	  - *What:* 1 minute on the iPhone 18 Pro in Apple Log.
871	  - *Measures:* VR-S1's log rule.
872	- **VR-B2 — `talking-head-iphone-hlg.mov`.**
873	  - *What:* 30 s on the iPhone 18 Pro in HDR (HLG).
874	  - *Measures:* VR-S1's HDR rule.
875	- **VR-C — the two-shot.**
876	  - *What:* two people seated side by side in one wide 16:9 shot for 2 minutes, with a mic each.
877	    It is the same session as bet 5's podcast sample: its wide camera and its mics.
878	  - *Measures:* VR-24's two-person rule, VR-S1 rule 6, VR6 and JOB-32 and JOB-37.
879	- **VR-D — a screen tutorial recorded in Frame Job after bet 2's sidecar.**
880	  - *What:* 2–3 minutes with the camera beside the screen, with clicks and typing.
881	  - *Measures:* VR5 and JOB-36.
882	- **VR-E — the owner's two lead-segment trial projects.**
883	  - *What:* the talking-head video and the screen tutorial cut in Frame Job, with word captions and
884	    a lower third, and each one's 16:9 export re-imported as one flattened clip.
885	  - *Measures:* VR3 and VR4 end to end; VR-S2's recall against the projects' own cut lists;
886	    JOB-35 and VR-38.
887	
888	**Synthetic** (`tools/proof/vr_fixtures.sh`). These use system-shipped art only, as the E9 spike's
889	fixtures do: Photos' bundled album covers with frontal faces, and Adobe CEP's person-at-desk image.
890	ffmpeg makes the videos, and nothing is read from a personal folder.
891	
892	- **f1:** one face panned along a known path across 1920 × 1080 for 20 s.
893	- **f2:** the face leaving frame for 2 s and returning.
894	- **f3:** two faces, first 400 px apart and then 1400 px apart.
895	- **f4:** three stills concatenated, with cuts at known frames.
896	- **f5:** a screen card with no person (`testsrc2` and text).
897	- **f6:** f1 at 4K, and f1 as a portrait clip with rotation metadata.
898	
899	Ground truth is the transform of the still's face box, detected once on the still. The script
900	refuses, as a scored failure, if Vision finds no face on a still. The core's tests need no video:
901	they read sample JSON written in the tests.
902	
903	### Risks
904	
905	- **Upscaled 1080p.** A 1080p source fills a 1080 × 1920 frame at ×1.78, which is visibly soft.
906	  Nothing hides it. The guide says to shoot 4K for vertical, and JOB-33 judges it.
907	- **Vision on log, dark or small faces.** VR-S1 measures it on the owner's footage. A face too small
908	  at 1280 px forces 1920, at analysis cost.
909	- **Results that move with macOS.** A new OS can change Vision's answers. The marker pins the
910	  request revisions and the OS build, so a new OS re-analyses on the next command. Proofs compare
911	  against the cache, not against a recomputation.
912	- **The wrong subject.** A poster on the wall, a face on a monitor, or an audience member can win
913	  VR-21's score. The hysteresis, the nudge and the Follow popup are the answers. A recording with a
914	  sidecar never follows faces (VR-51).
915	- **Composition inside existing actions.** A framing move inside an existing action is approximated
916	  by that action's curve. Coverage still holds (VR-7). Containment is measured in VR2's proof and in
917	  VR-S3.
918	- **Timeline clutter.** A long take gets many framing actions on its lane. Each is an ordinary
919	  action the person can delete.
920	- **Decoder budget.** Each "whole" clip adds a blurred copy that decodes the same file. The plan
921	  warns past 8 concurrent video tracks, and it does not refuse.
922	- **Track cap.** Backdrops share one track (VR-25). Only overlapping "whole" clips on different
923	  tracks need a second. At 64 the step is refused in the core's sentence, nothing is made, and the
924	  summary names it.
925	- **Graphics written by people or agents.** A graphic that does not lay itself out from
926	  `ctx.width` and `ctx.height` may overflow the tall frame. Only the bundled templates are fixed.
927	  The guide and `docs/graphics-api.md` say how.
928	- **Untimed or restyled captions** cannot be re-paged. They are kept, shrunk by `keep`, and counted.
929	- **Analysis time.** A one-hour recording at 5 Hz takes minutes even windowed. CJ1's sheet has
930	  Cancel, and the cache makes a second run free.
931	- **The copy drifts from the master.** That is by design until linked versions exist. JOB-35 says
932	  whether it matters.
933	- **Files at the cap.** `op_table.rs` (374 of 400) and `AppDelegate+Menus.swift` (554) take rows and
934	  items from every bet, so CJ0 pays their tolls first. `edit_action.rs` (595) must take nothing: if
935	  VR2 finds it needs a helper there, it pays a pure move first.
936	- **Linked versions are large.** VR7–VR9 touch every op that carries actions and the
937	  recipe-and-plan seam. The owner's yes at VR7 is the gate, and VR-S4 runs before the code.
938	
939	### Not in this bet
940	
941	- Stacked, side-by-side and corner-bubble layouts, and moving the recorded camera (bet 6). VR uses
942	  them once they exist.
943	- Switching between camera angles by speaker (bet 5). VR6 frames one wide shot only.
944	- Masks, cutouts or any per-pixel subject work. Framing uses boxes alone.
945	- Following clips inside a nest, matte pairs, or rotated clips. They are kept and listed.
946	- A language model or cloud model choosing the framing, and Apple FoundationModels.
947	- Motion blur on pans, stabilisation and optical-flow retiming. These are lifted non-goals, not
948	  scheduled here.
949	- Platform safe-zone overlays and named platform export rows (the next tier's publish slice).
950	- A range of the timeline as a vertical version. That is FC's New Project from Range or Make Short,
951	  followed by this step.
952	- Keyframes. Framing is actions, per §2's idea 3.
953

1	## Shared ground — CJ0 and shared infrastructure
2	
3	This is the part of road map "creator-jobs" (`designs/creator-jobs.md`) that no single bet owns:
4	the scope and the record (CJ0), the key rule, and the infrastructure two or more bets would
5	otherwise build twice or collide on. The six bets (TX transcript, CU cursor and recorder, VR
6	vertical, FC find clips, SW switch by speaker, CO cutout and layouts) are designed elsewhere;
7	this section names what they depend on and in what order they run. Line counts are `wc -l` at
8	`d0661e5d` (main, 2026-11-01).
9	
10	### Goal
11	
12	A person gets three things from the shared phases directly, and everything else through the
13	bets:
14	
15	- **Honest AI controls.** A command that needs Claude or AssemblyAI is greyed out when its key is
16	  missing, and its tooltip says which key and where to set it. An agent's call is refused with
17	  the same sentence. Nothing falls back to a weaker on-device model.

470	### Spikes
471	
472	Each rule is fixed here, before its run. Instruments go in `tools/proof/creator_spike/`; each
473	run's `results.json` stores the SHA-256 of `creator-jobs.md` as `rule_sha256` (CAM-2's
474	precedent), and the verdict is recorded in the road map and in the decision named.
475	
476	- **CJ-S1 — The clip ceiling (at CJ0; decides CJ-9).** Question: how many clips can a project
477	  hold before editing, planning, drawing or undo stop being usable? Projects of N = 4,096, 8,192,
478	  16,384 and 32,768 one-second media clips over four tracks of one media, generated as packages.
479	  Measured: (1) `rc_project_apply` of `split` at the middle, median of 20; (2) `rc_project_from_json`
480	  plus `rc_composition_plan`; (3) `frame_recipe` at 20 random times, median; (4) in the Release app
481	  over MCP, one `ripple_delete_ranges` of 100 ranges and its undo; (5) the app's resident memory
482	  after 50 undo steps of `split`. N above 4,096 needs the bench to raise the cap in a scratch
483	  build only. **Rule:** N_max is the largest N for which (1) ≤ 50 ms, (2) ≤ 500 ms, (3) ≤ 2 ms,
484	  (4) applies in ≤ 1 s and undoes in ≤ 1 s, and (5) grows by at most a sixteenth of physical
485	  memory. N_max > 4,096 → CJ6 raises the ceiling to N_max; otherwise CJ-9 keeps 4,096.
486	- **CJ-S2 — Vision faces on this Mac (at CJ0 when S-TH1 exists, else at CJ3's start; decides
487	  CJ-30 and CJ-32).** Question: are face tracks deterministic, fast and found on the owner's
488	  material, and on which device and at what size? Inputs: S-TH1, S-TH2 (V-Log), a portrait iPhone
489	  file, and the moving-still fixture. Measured: (1) the cache bytes over three runs on each of
490	  CPU, GPU and Neural Engine; (2) the largest rectangle difference between devices; (3) seconds
491	  per minute of source at 10 samples a second, frames at long side 720, 1080 and 1440, faces
492	  alone and with landmarks; (4) the share of samples with a face over S-TH1's first 60 s, which
493	  its recording brief makes front-facing; (5) on S-TH2, that share on the raw log picture and on
494	  the converted one; (6) peak memory. **Rules:** the device is the fastest whose three runs are
495	  byte-identical, else STOP and the kind's stamp carries a tolerance instead of bytes (an
496	  amendment before CJ3's code); the frame size is the smallest whose face share is within 1
497	  percentage point of 1440's; the sample rate stays 10 a second if faces with landmarks run at
498	  ≥ 4× realtime at that size, else 5; landmarks stay in `faces` if they cost ≤ 2× faces alone,
499	  else mouth opening becomes its own kind, asked only by SW; (4) below 95 % is STOP; (5) picks the
500	  arm with the higher share, a tie going to the converted picture.
501	- **CJ-S3 — The lane's reader and width (at CJ2a's start; decides CJ-21 and CJ-23).** Question:
502	  what does decoding for analysis cost, and does a second concurrent job pay? Measured on a 4K
503	  HEVC 10-bit file and a 1080p H.264 file: frames a second through the scaled direct reader and
504	  through the converted path; total throughput of one job and of two; and `play_preview`'s frames
505	  composed over 10 s of a 1080p timeline while each runs, against idle. **Rules:** width 2 only
506	  if two jobs reach ≥ 1.5× one job's throughput AND `play_preview` composes ≥ 95 % of its idle
507	  count; the converted path only for converting media, unless it is within 10 % of the direct
508	  reader, when it is used for all.

926	- **Canned analyses:** JSON `faces` and subject tracks with known motion, a jump, two faces and an
927	  exit, honoured under CJ-26 (VR's and SW's planners, byte-exact).
928	- **Masks:** a moving disc as a mask sequence (CO's compositor rows, independent of Vision).
929	- **Cursor sidecar:** a synthetic sidecar over `testsrc` (CU's and VR's rows).
930	- **Clip-count projects:** generated packages of N clips (CJ-S1, CJ6).
931	- **Key states:** empty and dummy-key scratch secret folders with the two stand-in servers (CJ1).
932	
933	**How Vision-dependent proofs stay deterministic.** (1) A planner's rows run on canned analyses
934	and assert bytes. (2) Vision's rows on real samples assert tolerances fixed before the run and
935	never exact numbers. (3) A determinism row compares two runs on the pinned device, byte for byte.
936	(4) A proof compares against the cache, never against a recomputation. (5) Every stamp carries
937	the OS build and the compute device, and every results file records both. (6) What only a person
938	can judge — whether a reframe, a cutout or a switch looks right on real footage — is a JOB row.
939	
940	### Risks
941	
942	- **Vision moves under the app.** An OS update or another compute device changes the numbers; the
943	  stamp makes that a re-analysis rather than a mix, and proofs read caches. A change in Vision's
944	  request revisions is a kind-version bump.
945	- **The Neural Engine is shared.** Analysis can slow playback, export and `AUSoundIsolation`'s
946	  renders; the lane is width 1 at `.utility` until CJ-S3 shows otherwise.
947	- **Log and HDR footage.** Faces and masks on a flat log picture may miss; CJ-S2 picks the arm.
948	- **The clip ceiling and undo memory.** Each edit keeps a whole project handle, so TX's word cuts
949	  and SW's switching press on memory before they press on 4,096; CJ-S1 measures both.
950	- **Five tabs at 280 pt** are 56 pt each; "Transcript" and "Document" may not fit (TX's decision).
951	- **The helper is shared with Rasterize.** FC's Claude ranking goes through `agent/` (AI-1), whose
952	  source is held byte-identical with Rasterize's; any new helper command is a change offered to
953	  both.
954	- **Ad-hoc signatures and TCC.** Input Monitoring, like Screen Recording, is lost at every
955	  `make app`; the granted tiers are manual checks.
956	- **Lanes collide on tables.** The frozen files' wiring lines, menus, `UIMenuTable.swift`,
957	  `inventory.json`, `menus-and-shortcuts.md`, the decision file and the spec index's Lines cells
958	  all take rows from three lanes; the integrator resolves them one landing at a time, and T8 moves
959	  the busiest one out of a frozen file.
960	- **Provisional format numbers.** CU, SW, CO and VR (linked versions) each may bump; renumbering at
961	  landing is the integrator's (CJ-6).
962	- **The key rule may surprise.** A person with cached transcripts and no key keeps Remove Filler
963	  Words (CJ-12); one with neither sees it greyed, with a tooltip instead of a sheet.
964	- **Copying caches into a derived project** could duplicate AssemblyAI clean-up state; CJ-51 copies
965	  transcripts and never pending deletions.
966	- **Samples may not come.** Every phase runs on fixtures and skips real-sample rows by name; the
967	  quality claims then rest on JOB rows alone.
968	- **The samples are personal.** They hold the owner's face and voice; they are never committed,
969	  and no live cloud proof sends them without its explicit flags and the month's budget (P-3, P-6).
970	- **The trial may reorder the road map** (CJ-5); an amendment to CJ-2 records it.
971	- **Unmeasured playback.** Several 4K angles and multi-hour timelines have no figure yet (survey
972	  decision 8); SW's first spike.
973	
974	### Not in this bet
975	
976	- The six bets themselves, and every analysis kind only one bet needs: subjects, saliency and
977	  human rectangles (VR), person masks (CO), sound classes (FC), cursor data (CU).
978	- The survey's next tier: Proposals and Recipes, Punch in on cuts, a source viewer with skimming,
979	  In and Out on media and favourite ranges (CJ4 is only the op arguments), caption styles and a
980	  brand kit, the publish polish slice, `search_media`, merging the tutorials, optical-flow slow
981	  motion, WebVTT import.
982	- Everything in the survey's "Not worth chasing" table.
983	- An on-device language model (FoundationModels), an on-device filler pass, a Frame Job-run relay
984	  or account (C2, #125 stays iced), and the Keychain for keys (R6-5's measured reason stands).
985	- Any other platform, a plugin system, stabilisation, motion blur, optical-flow retiming and
986	  proxies: allowed by CJ-1, not scheduled.
987	- Any change to what a decision made under the old non-goals decides, unless a bet's phase
988	  amends it in writing.

- **FC-71 — Find Clips is a window of its own per document, not a sheet,** so the person can play,
  scrub and edit while reading the list. An edit to the project marks a shown ranking "made
  before the last edit" and offers Rank again; its spans are not remapped.
- **FC-72 — A row's Play sets the In–Out range to its span and plays it looped** (View ▸ Loop's
  path, `applyLoopRange`). The timeline's candidate wash carries each ranked moment's number.
- **FC-73 — `find_clips` answers `ranking` while FC-66's cache is current,** else null.
- **FC-80 — Make Short is, per span, in this order:**
  1. `keep_range` into a new document (FC-20, FC-21, FC-22).
  2. Fillers: one `ripple_delete_ranges` of `FillerDetector`'s spans, "Remove Filler Words".
  3. The vertical step (FC9).
  4. Captions: `transcribe` with the chosen word style and `replace: true`.
  5. Save to the chosen folder, queue the export, close the document.

  Fillers come before the vertical step so the framing follows the final cut, and captions
  come last so their pages measure on the final canvas.
- **FC-81 — Make Short never sends audio anywhere.** Captions come from a carried cloud
  transcript, which needs no request, or else from the on-device engine. Fillers are cut only
  where a carried transcript was asked for disfluencies (TR-7 stands); otherwise the step is
  skipped and the short's note says why. R6-2 stands.
- **FC-82 — Shorts are saved, exported and closed.** Make Short asks for a folder once. Each short
  is `<source stem> — <rank or n> <title>.framejob` and `.mp4` there, a taken name gaining
  " 2", " 3"…. It is exported with the chosen Export row (H.264 MP4 at the canvas size, −14 LUFS,
  by default) through the Export Queue and closed once queued, so 30 shorts never hold 30 windows.
- **FC-83 — `make_short {from, to, folder, name?, shape?, captions?, look?, remove_fillers?,
  export?}` mirrors the Make Short sheet** for one span. `export` takes the `export` tool's keys
  but `path`. It runs off main, never asks, and answers the short's path, its `export_id` and the
  steps that ran or were skipped. It is ask-first for the assistant (amends AI-7).
- **FC-84 — File ▸ Make Short from Range… runs the same sheet over the In–Out range, with no key.**
- **FC-90 — The vertical step is bet 3's planner applied to the short's own document as one undo
  step,** with the shape 9:16 by default, 1:1 or Keep. Before bet 3's planner lands, only Keep
  exists, and `shape` other than `keep` is refused: "Vertical shorts need Make Vertical Version,
  which this build does not have yet."
- **FC-91 — The owner's verdict on Find Clips**, recorded after FC9's trial, as GR-9 recorded
  grading's.

- **What a person gets:** Make Short's Shape row (9:16, 1:1, Keep) becomes live. Each short is

when the road map closes:
- **A multicam source kind** (one clip holding every angle, as Final Cut Pro's): the program
  track does the same jobs with ordinary clips (SW-10, SW-90).
- **Proxies:** only if SW-S2 shows a shortfall, as a Performance-project issue.
- **Virtual angles from one wide camera** (cropping to each face): bet 3's subject tracking can
  supply the framing; a candidate after VR.
- **Laughter to the wide shot:** needs Find Clips' Sound Analysis cache; a candidate after FC.
- **Telling speakers apart by voice on one microphone with no faces** (diarization): Apple's
  frameworks have no on-device diarization; AssemblyAI's speaker labels would make it a
  masks; a Mac that regenerates them may draw a slightly different edge. Proofs compare against
  cached masks.
- **Layouts against existing placement.** A switch replaces the placement of later clips up to the
  next switch; a hand-placed camera there is overwritten. Zooms and punch-ins are refused and
  nested (CO-62), and a nested screen loses rounded corners, because a nest clip's radius reaches
  no layer (`nest.rs:382`).
- **Bet interactions.** Bet 1's cuts split every unlocked track, which CO-61's propagation
  handles. Bet 1 shows words inside a nest as not editable, and CO-62 may nest picture clips; it
  never nests the microphone. Bet 2's cursor layer must ride with the screen clip or its nest, or
  layouts will separate them. Bet 3's vertical version should use `stacked` for screen-and-camera
  pairs rather than reframing each clip.
- **API drift.** If Apple deprecates the `VN*` segmentation classes in favour of the `async`-only
  Swift API (as `NSCursor.currentSystem` was deprecated), the analyser needs the `async`
  confinement W-8 allows, in `MediaImporter.swift` or a decision that widens it.
- **Licences.** Concat, Cap and OpenScreen code, shaders and models are not opened or carried over.

content.content:
- **AU-83 — ⌥-press on the line adds a point, as an action.** At the press's clip time snapped to
  the frame, t: inside an action A whose end names ONLY `audio.volume` (no other group, no other
  audio key), A is split at t — A shortened to `t − A.start`, a new action `[t, A.end)` ending at
  A's end volume and carrying A's curve when it is not linear — and the point dragged is A's new
  end, starting at the evaluated volume at t; a press under one frame from A's start beeps (a
  zero-length action is refused, and a live edit swallows refusals). For a linear A the click
  alone leaves what is heard unchanged; for an eased A both halves carry its curve, so the values
  at t and at A's end are kept and the shape between is re-eased on each side. Inside any other
  action or one a trim left running past the clip's end (`add_action` would refuse the split's
  second half), or under one frame after the latest action end at or before t (any kind: actions never
  overlap), a beep and nothing. Otherwise a new action `[prevEnd, t)` (prevEnd that latest end,
  else 0; the core's default curve, linear) ending at the evaluated volume at t, so the click alone
  changes nothing heard. The new id is the base's `next_id`. The click adds the point at once; the
  drag continues as AU-82 on that end; one undo step, "Add Volume Point".

- **AU-110 — A duck can follow the ducking clip's SPEECH, from spans saved on its media

  (`foundations.md`).** `audio.duck.mode` is `extent` (the default, today's behaviour byte for

  sorted, non-overlapping, `0 ≤ start < end ≤ duration`, at most `MAX_SPEECH_SPANS` (100,000),
  written by the op `set_media_speech {media, spans}` (document-level, refused inside a scope as

wide is optional and is the angle no microphone names, when exactly one is left. The range is
  the In/Out range when set, else the span every angle covers. A microphone's steps outside its
  own clip count as silent. The switch trusts the placement; it does not check sync, and the
  guide says to run Synchronize Audio first.
- **SW-21 — A microphone is active when its voice is its own.** On a 10 ms timeline grid over
  the range, for each microphone m: its level ℓ_m(k) is 10·log10 of the loudness cache's
  K-weighted mean square, through the clip's own channel matrix (AU-35) and source map,
  averaged over 100 ms; its voice v_m(k) is the speech cache's probability for the 32 ms chunk
  holding that step's source time. P_m, its own speech level, is the 90th percentile of ℓ_m over
  steps with v_m ≥ 0.5 (a person's own voice is the loudest thing on their microphone); F_m, its
  floor, is the 10th percentile over steps with v_m < 0.5. m is active at k when v_m(k) ≥ 0.5,
  ℓ_m(k) ≥ P_m − `bleed_db` (default 15 dB) and ℓ_m(k) ≥ F_m + 6 dB. When two or more are
  active and one's ℓ − P exceeds every other's by `dominance_db` (default 8 dB), only it is
  active. The four numbers are provisional until SW-S4 sets them.
- **SW-22 — Turns become shots.** One active microphone is that person; two or more is
  crosstalk; none is nobody. A person's turn bridges their gaps under 0.5 s. A turn shorter than
  `min_turn` (1.0 s) starts no shot. Crosstalk lasting `crosstalk_min` (1.0 s) or longer shows
  the wide, or holds the current shot when there is no wide or `crosstalk` is `hold`. Nobody
  holds the current shot. A new shot starts `lead` (0.2 s) before the turn's first active step,
  snapped to the frame grid. A shot shorter than `min_shot` (2.0 s) is merged into the shot
  before it (the first shot into the one after). The range opens on the wide when there is one,
  else on the first speaker. An optional `wide_after` (off by default) cuts to the wide for
  `min_shot` once one person has held the screen that long.
- **SW-23 — What the switch writes, as one undo step "Switch by Speaker".** A new front track
  named "Program"; one `copy_pieces` per angle with that angle's shot ranges and
  `audio: false`; each angle track hidden (`set_track {hidden: true}`) when every clip on it in
  the range is an angle, else each such angle clip's picture switched off; and, when "Mute the
  cameras' own sound" is on, `set_enabled {audio: false}` on every angle that is not also a
  microphone. That box defaults on when no microphone is an angle. Microphones are never edited.
  With `track` (the sheet's "Replace the shots on"), the switch writes onto that track, after a
  `lift_range`-style clear of it alone over the range, instead of adding one.
- **SW-24 — It refuses, naming every reason at once (SY-1's form).** Fewer than two angles; a
  speaker without a microphone; one microphone for two or more speakers ("each person needs
  their own microphone" until SW8); a microphone whose loudness or speech is still being
  analysed; a microphone in which no speech was found; an angle that does not cover the range;
  and a result that would pass `MAX_CLIPS` ("Switch by Speaker would add N clips to M; the most
  is 4,096 — raise the minimum shot").
- **SW-25 — The switch reads caches and computes nothing else.** The loudness and speech caches
  are read through the clip (its source map, channel matrix and, after SW4, its audio source);

  `SpeakerSwitch.swift`, probe-callable, readings in and shots or refusals out.
- **SW-26 — The sheet and the tool take the same arguments.** `switch_by_speaker {speakers:

content.content:
### 3. Make Vertical Version

**Pitch.** File ▸ Make Vertical Version… writes a 9:16 or 1:1 version of a finished 16:9 edit. Each clip fills the frame and follows the face, person or salient region that Vision found on the Mac. It does this with ordinary eased x, y and scale actions the creator can nudge. In a screen recording made after bet 2, it follows the cursor instead. Captions re-lay for the short side, and graphics re-layout from the canvas size. A shot that cannot be cropped gets Add Blurred Background.

**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** Subject-tracking reframe is table stakes. OpusClip [C11], CapCut [C4], Premiere [P21], Final Cut Pro for iPad [P17], Riverside [C9], Kapwing [C20] and Screen Studio [S1] all ship it, and auto-repurposing is the most-wanted creator AI feature in one survey [D2]. Frame Job pulls ahead on terms. CapCut moved Auto Reframe behind Pro in April 2026 [C4]. Here it is free and local, and the result is editable pan actions rather than a render. If the owner chooses linked versions (one cut, with a framing per shape), Frame Job is ahead of every rival, because their vertical copies drift from the master.

**Builds on.** `fill_scale` (`edit_fit.rs`); Add Blurred Background (`edit_background.rs`); word captions sized to the shorter side (`CaptionStyle.swift`); graphics that read `ctx.canvas`; actions (`edit_action.rs`); nests (`edit_nest.rs`); `set_canvas` (`edit_canvas.rs`); File ▸ Duplicate; the E9 Vision spike in `tools/proof/effects_spike/`.

**Effort.** M as a regenerated copy. L for linked versions, which need a canvas per version, framing overrides per clip and a format bump.

**Risks and what comes first.**
- Spec §1 lists auto-reframe as a non-goal, so a §11 decision must lift it first. The reason given there, heavy pixel work outside the one-pass compositor, no longer applies: the analysis runs offline and its output is actions.
- No two actions on one clip may overlap, of any kind. A clip that already carries an action (a zoom, a grade, a ramp) needs a wrapping nest, and a nest's canvas freezes at the size it was nested at.
- `set_canvas` does not rescale action end states. A screencast's existing zoom actions keep their 16:9 targets, and the planner must rewrite them.
- `MediaCacheLane` is a width-2 lane for audio decodes, so video analysis needs its own lane, cache kind and ledger rows.
- The planner should use face, human and saliency rectangles with tracking, not masks: the E9 spike found that foreground masks flicker on video.
- Two people in frame, a speaker leaving the frame, and shot changes inside one flattened clip each need a rule.

### 4. Find Clips
## Decisions for the owner

1. **Lead segment.** Recommendation: creators who record themselves talking, meaning talking-head YouTube and screen tutorials (bets 1, 2 and 6). Then repurposing to shorts (bets 3 and 4), then video podcasts (bet 5).
2. **Which spec §1 non-goals to lift, and how far.**
   - Auto-reframe: needed for bet 3.
   - Multicam: narrowly, as speaker switching on stacked tracks, or fully, as a multicam clip with an angle grid (bet 5).
   - ML and heavy pixel work: needed for camera cutout (issue #124's D5, bet 6).
   - Optical-flow retiming and motion blur: stay out until a spike.
   - A plugin system: stays out.
3. **Which spec §11 decisions to amend before code.**
   - TR-3, AI-6 and W-9, so that a deterministic retake pass may strike words (bet 1).
   - `recording.md`: cursor as data, callouts, a source kind and a schema bump (bet 2).
   - AI-10, for Proposals.
   - W-10, for inspector caption styling.
4. **Shortcut capture.** Whether the recorder may ask for the Input Monitoring grant, with capture opt-in and limited to modifier shortcuts by default.
5. **Vertical versions.** A regenerated copy (M), or linked versions in one project, where one cut has a framing per shape (L, with a format bump).
6. **Language models.** Claude on the creator's key only, or Apple FoundationModels as a no-key fallback. FoundationModels needs Apple Intelligence on and has a context of about 4k tokens.
7. **Cloud.** Confirm that bring-your-own key stays the only cloud model. Then either accept that filler detection stays AssemblyAI-only (TR-7), or fund an on-device filler pass.
8. **Performance.** Allow one measurement of multi-stream 4K and multi-hour playback now, despite the features-first order, before bet 5 and before any claim to lead. Add proxies only if the measurement falls short.
9. **Real use.** Cut at least one real video per lead segment in Frame Job before or alongside the first bet, so the bets are tested against real work.
10. **Positioning.** Whether to present Frame Job to creators as free, open, on-device and credit-free. That position answers the most common switching triggers: price rises [C5] [S7] [D19], metered credits [D7] [P7] and content-licence scares [D18].

content.content:
# Frame Job User Guide

Frame Job is a native macOS video editor for Apple Silicon Macs running
macOS 26 or later. You open a movie, arrange it on layered tracks over a fixed
canvas, then trim, cut, grade, caption, animate and export it. Every edit you
make in the window can also be made by an AI agent over MCP, or by the built-in
Assistant.

The quickest way in: **File ▸ Open…** (⌘O) on a movie makes an untitled project
sized and timed to it, with the movie on Track 1, ready to cut. Save writes a
`.framejob` package.

## The pages

Read the first four in order to learn the editor; the rest stand alone.

1. [Projects and media](projects-and-media.md) — starting, saving and opening projects, the `.framejob` package, the Document tab's canvas settings, importing files, the Media tab and relinking.
2. [The timeline and playback](timeline.md) — the editor window, tracks and their switches, the ruler and playhead, zoom, selection, snapping, markers, the in/out range and playback.
3. [Editing clips](editing.md) — placing, moving, trimming, slipping, splitting, deleting and closing gaps, copy and paste, and nests.
4. [Canvas, layers, text and shapes](canvas-and-layers.md) — placing a picture on the canvas, opacity, blend modes, shadows and filters, text, shape, image and background clips, and matte tracks.
5. [Motion, actions and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md) — actions that animate a clip's properties over time, motion presets, and transitions between clips.
6. [Speed, reverse and freeze frames](speed.md) — constant speed, fitting a clip to a length, rate stretch, speed ramps and their presets, reversing and freeze frames.
7. [Audio](audio.md) — clip levels, fades and their shapes, ducking by clip length or by speech, noise reduction, compression, pan, mute and solo, Normalize and Synchronize Audio.
8. [Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words](cleanup-tools.md) — cutting dead air and filler words out of a spoken recording in one step.
9. [Captions and transcription](captions.md) — importing and exporting captions, and transcribing speech on this Mac or with AssemblyAI into subtitles or word-by-word captions.
10. [Colour grading](color-grading.md) — the Color tab, wheels, curves, looks and LUTs, adjustment clips and qualifiers, Show Ungraded and the scopes.
11. [HDR and colour management](hdr-and-color.md) — how sources are read, camera log, SDR and HDR (HLG) projects, blending, and HDR and SDR deliverables.
12. [Motion graphics](graphics.md) — graphic clips, the built-in graphics, their properties in the inspector, and bringing in your own.
13. [Screen recording](screen-recording.md) — recording a display or a window with system audio, microphone and click rings, recording a camera on its own or beside the screen, and recording voice-overs.
14. [Exporting](export.md) — the export sheet, its formats and settings, presets, the Export Queue, and saving single frames.

## Bet 3 — Make Vertical Version with on-device subject tracking

### Goal

A creator finishes a 16:9 edit and chooses **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…**. Frame Job opens a
copy of the project at 9:16 (1080 × 1920 from a 1080p canvas, 2160 × 3840 from a 4K one) or 1:1.
In the copy:

- every full-frame picture fills the tall frame and follows the face, the person or the salient
  region that Vision found on the Mac, as eased x, y and scale actions on the clip's own action
  lane, which the creator selects and nudges on the canvas like any other action;
- a shot with nothing to follow (a screen, a landscape, a two-shot too wide to crop) is shown
  whole over a blurred copy of itself;
- a cut inside a clip (an export of another edit, imported as one file) is a hard cut in the
  framing too;
- word captions are paged again for the narrow frame from their own words, so corrections made
  by hand survive, and subtitles take the narrow frame's measure;
- a graphic that filled the 16:9 frame is re-sized to the tall one and lays itself out again;
- a background plate or blurred backdrop that filled the 16:9 frame fills the tall one;
- every other layer (a camera bubble, a title, a logo) keeps its relative place;
- existing zooms keep what they showed: each is composed with the framing, never left aiming at
  16:9 targets.

The same planner is a command on its own: **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…** frames the selected clips on
the canvas they are on (a 4K talking head on a 1080p canvas, a 16:9 clip dropped into a vertical
project). After bet 2, a screen recording's vertical version follows the cursor. After bet 5, a
two-person wide shot follows whoever is speaking. Later, if the owner chooses, one project holds
several **framings** of one cut (linked versions), so a trim in the 16:9 cut is a trim in the 9:16
one.

Nothing is uploaded, nothing needs a key, and every result is an ordinary undo step and an MCP
tool.

### Owner's answers applied

- **"Add all: 1-6."** Bet 3 is in the road map "creator-jobs", prefix VR.
- **"Remove all explicit non-goals."** Spec §1's "auto-reframe (heavy pixel work or ML, outside the
  compositor's one-pass shape)" is lifted by CJ-1. This bet supplies the sentence that names where
  it went (VR-1). Lifting it schedules nothing beyond what is below. Motion blur on pans,
  stabilisation and optical flow stay unscheduled here.
- **"Anything that requires significant AI should require that the user has supplied a key."**
  Nothing in this bet uses a language model or a cloud model. Vision's rectangle and saliency
  requests are on-device Apple frameworks that run today without a key, so under CJ-3 they are not
  "significant AI" and no VR control is ever disabled for a missing key (VR-2). If a later phase
  wanted a model to choose framing by meaning, it would fall under CJ-3; none does.
- **"The recorder can ask for input monitoring."** Bet 2's (CJ-4). VR5 reads typing bursts from
  bet 2's sidecar when present and works without them.
- **"Cutting one real video per lead segment … alongside the first bet. OK."** The trial's two
  videos (CJ-5's T1, a talking head from S-TH1, and T2, a screen tutorial from S-ST1) are this
  bet's end-to-end material. Their vertical versions, watched on a phone, are the bet's own trial
  (JOB-35), recorded as VR-38 the way GR-9 recorded grading's. That verdict also answers the
  linked-versions question at VR7a.
- **The owner did not choose between a regenerated copy and linked versions** (survey decision 5,
  left by CJ-2 to the phase that needs it). The recommendation (VR-3) is the copy first (VR1–VR4,
  no format bump), with the planner's output shaped so that linked versions (VR7a–VR9, a format
  bump) reuse it unchanged. Linked versions are asked at VR7a, after the trial.
- **The orchestrator's defaults, each of which the owner can change:**
  - VR runs in lane C (CJ's lane plan), after CJ2b, CJ3 and CJ5, in the order VR1 → VR2a → VR2b
    → VR3 → VR4.
  - VR5 waits for CU's sidecar phase (lane B) and then runs next in lane C. VR6 waits for SW2,

### How it fits the tree

**Placement and the canvas.**
- Spec §5.3 and `core/src/edit_zoom.rs` (467) :38–55 give the one placement rule (★): `canvas(q)
  = anchor + s·R(θ)·(c + q)`. `video.x` and `video.y` are canvas pixels from the canvas centre,
  `scale` is uniform, and a region is in source pixels from the cropped rect's centre. The module
  doc also solves (★) for a region with rotation and the `SCALE_MAX` clamp. The reframe arithmetic
  is a second solution of the same equation and cites it.
- `core/src/edit_fit.rs` (61) :52 `fill_scale` is `max(cw/sw, ch/sh)` clamped to `SCALE_MAX`. A
  1920 × 1080 picture on a 1080 × 1920 canvas fills at ×1.778, so the tall frame sees a window
  607.5 px wide of the 1920 (31.6 %). On 1:1 it sees 1080 of 1920 (56 %). A 1080p source is
  therefore upscaled ×1.78 in a 1080 × 1920 export, and a 4K source is downscaled ×0.89.
- `core/src/edit_canvas.rs` (251) :58–96: `set_canvas`'s `rescale_clips` multiplies top-level
  `x`, `y` by their own axis ratio and `scale` by the smaller ratio, and **does not rescale action
  end patches** ("an animated move on a resized canvas therefore keeps its old target"). It never
  touches nested clips (a nest's canvas is frozen: `core/src/model.rs` (570) :392,
  `core/src/edit_nest.rs` (338) :223). Spec §6c :150 says the same.
- `core/src/model_query.rs` (551) :217 `source_size`: a media, still or image clip's size is the
  media record's (the displayed, oriented size); a nest's is its frozen canvas; text has none.

**Actions, speed and motion.**
- Spec §5.4 and `core/src/edit_action.rs` (595, at the cap) :63 `overlapping_action`: no two
  actions on one clip may overlap, of any kind. Volume-line points are actions on the same list
  (AU-80), so an ordinary A/V clip often already carries actions.
- An action's x, y and scale interpolate together with one curve (`Curve`: linear, ease_in,
  ease_out, ease_in_out; `core/src/model.rs` :452). The set of placements that cover a canvas is
  an intersection of half-spaces in (x, y, scale), so it is convex. A lerp of two covering states
  on one curve covers at every frame between them. The coverage guarantee in VR-7 rests on this.
- `core/src/edit_split.rs` (284) :204–246 is how a straddled action is cut: the head ends at the
  evaluated state at the cut narrowed to the keys the action named (`state_patch` :40,
  `narrow_to` :61), the tail keeps the original end, both keep the curve, and a `speed` head's end
  rate is solved separately (SR-18 (e)). VR2b splits actions the same way (VR-27).
- **Source time to clip time.** `core/src/speed_map.rs` (414) `SpeedMap::of` (:215) answers a map
  only for a ramped clip; a constant-speed clip has none. `source_at` (:295) answers source ticks
  read since `in` and does not reflect a reversal; neither does `Project::source_map`
  (`core/src/speed_segments.rs` (274) :243–273). The one place the core maps a FILE time into a
  clip's own time with reversal, speed and ramps together is `speech_in_clip`
  (`core/src/audio_duck_speech.rs` (193) :31–67): reflect over `media.duration` when the clip is
  reversed (`in` is measured in the reversed stream), subtract `in`, then `SpeedMap::time_at` when
  ramped, else divide by the base speed. VR2a extracts that mapping into one helper (VR-20). Swift
  reads the other direction through `SourceMap.swift` (`rc_project_source_map`, SR-20) and
  `ReverseMirror.swift`.
- **`video.motion`** (`core/src/motion.rs` (492) :1–30, `core/src/model_motion.rs` (206)
  :175–206): a preset's scale factor F, rotation φ and offset Δ are applied at `recipe.rs`'s
  `moved` on top of the evaluated placement, so a motion moves the drawn layer after the actions.
  `fade` changes only opacity. The other arrivals and departures (`zoom_in`, `zoom_out`, the four
  slides, `spin`, `pop`) and every During motion (`pulse`, `shake`, `spin`, `bounce`, `drift`) move
  or turn the layer. VR-7 states what that does to the coverage guarantee.

**Why not a wrapping nest.**
- `core/src/format.rs` (250) :27–28, :57–61: `MAX_TRACKS` is 64 and counts every nest's tracks.
  One nest per clip that carries an action costs at least one track each, so a 40-clip edit with

  properties reach no layer (spec §5.3).
- A nest takes a default cross dissolve in place of the clip's own transition (`edit_nest.rs`
  :229–232).
- So this bet makes no nest (VR-6). The framing is composed into the clip's own placement and
  actions instead.

**Bet-level, recorded at CJ0.**

- **VR-1 — Auto-reframe is in, as analysis plus ordinary actions.** Subjects are found offline by
  Vision's rectangle and saliency requests on the Mac and cached per media in CJ's analysis store.
  The core plans the framing, and the result is placement and actions on the clip. No mask, no
  shipped model, and no pixel work outside the one-pass compositor. *The sentence for CJ0's §1
  history line:* "Auto-reframe was lifted with the rest by §11 CJ-1; File ▸ Make Vertical Version
  and Clip ▸ Follow Subject find faces, people and salient regions with Vision on the Mac and
  write ordinary actions (§11 VR-1)."
- **VR-2 — Bet 3 needs no key.** Vision's requests are on-device Apple frameworks, outside CJ-3's
  key rule for language and cloud models. No VR control is disabled for a missing key.
- **VR-3 — A regenerated copy first; linked versions designed and asked at VR7a.** The copy needs
  no format change and is the material for the owner's trial. The planner answers a framing path,
  a similarity per instant from the source canvas to the target canvas. The copy composes it into
  each clip. Linked versions would store it per framing. If the owner says no at VR7a, VR7a–VR9
  are filed as one issue with this design.
- **VR-4 — Subjects are boxes, detected per sample, never tracked by Vision.** Faces come from
  CJ3's `faces` kind (CJ-30). People (`VNDetectHumanRectanglesRequest` r2, `upperBodyOnly` false)
  and salient regions (`VNGenerateAttentionBasedSaliencyImageRequest` r2) come from VR1's
  `subjects` kind. Each sample gets a fresh `VNImageRequestHandler`; `VNTrackObjectRequest` and
  every `VNStatefulRequest` are out, so a sample's boxes depend on that frame alone. Linking boxes
  across samples is CJ-31's arithmetic; choosing among them is the core's (VR-21). Masks are out
  for framing because E9 measured them flickering.
- **VR-5 — The planner is the core's, and `reframe_clip` is an op (CJ-8 (f)).** Swift measures
  (decode, Vision) and caches. The core maps samples into the clip's time, chooses subjects, plans
  the path, enforces coverage and writes actions. It is an op rather than a composite because two
  rules must hold inside the core: coverage (VR-7), which needs (★) and `fill_scale`, and
  composition into existing action ends (VR-27), which needs the actions' own evaluation — the
  reason `edit_background.rs`'s module doc gives for `add_blurred_background` being an op. The op
  is a pure function of the project and the samples handed to it, as `ripple_delete_ranges` is of
  Remove Silences' spans.
- **VR-6 — No nest is made to make room for framing.** Framing is composed into the clip's own
  base placement and actions (VR-27). A nest would cost tracks against `MAX_TRACKS` and would wall
  the clip off from blurred backgrounds, filler cuts and the transcript.
- **VR-7 — A followed picture never shows the canvas, with three named exceptions.** The planner's
  window always lies inside the clip's picture: scale is at least fill and the offsets are clamped
  by (★). Every key the planner writes is a covering state, and one curve carries x, y and scale,
  so every frame between keys covers too. The exceptions:
  - **`fit` spans.** A clip framed `fit`, or a `where_empty: fit` span, shows the whole picture,
    so the canvas shows around it. With `backdrop` the op puts a blurred copy behind each such
    span, so nothing of the canvas shows; without it the canvas shows, as Fit does today. A nest
    clip has no blurred copy (VR-26).
  - **Motion.** A clip whose `video.motion` moves or turns the layer keeps its motion. The
    guarantee holds on the evaluated placement and excludes the motion's span: an arrival's or a
    departure's span after the tent, and the whole clip for a During motion. A `spin` (either slot)
    is treated as rotation (VR-26). `fade` moves nothing and is not an exception.
  - **Opacity.** Fades, transitions and opacity below 1 are the author's and are not the
    framing's to cover.

**VR1 — subjects.**

- **VR-10 — `subjects`, one analysis kind holding people and salient regions.** Per sample: each
  person box (`VNDetectHumanRectanglesRequest` r2, `upperBodyOnly` false) with its confidence, and
  each salient box (`VNGenerateAttentionBasedSaliencyImageRequest` r2) with its confidence, both
  from one decode, so the two requests cost one read of the file. The request revisions are in the
  kind's version. Stored in CJ-22's store and frame: `cache/analysis/subjects/<media id>.json`,
  runs in media source ticks, each box as its centre and size normalised 0…1 in display
  orientation, origin top-left. No sibling folder (CJ-8 (c)).
- **VR-11 — The grid, the reader and the device are CJ3's.** `subjects` samples fall on the
  `faces` grid (CJ-30's rate, after CJ-S2), or on every other `faces` sample if VR-S1 rule 1 says
  so, so a planner merges the two kinds by time with no resampling. Frames come through CJ-23's
  reader at `faces`' long side unless VR-S1 rule 2 moves it. The compute device is CJ-32's pin.
  Person boxes are linked across samples by CJ-31's rule, through CJ3's own linker (one
  implementation); salient boxes are not linked. Values are stored raw.
- **VR-12 — What a VR command analyses.** For each media a clip shows, the windows the clips play
  plus 1 s each side, in this order: `shots`, then `faces`, then `subjects`, so face and person
  ids restart at cached cuts (CJ-31). CJ-20 stands: nothing runs at import.
- **VR-13 — View ▸ Show Subjects is a per-window view state that draws only what is cached.** It
  draws the selected clip's face, person and salient boxes at the playhead, picked by the
  playhead's source time through `SourceMap` and `ReverseMirror`, and placed on the canvas by
  `ProjectSnapshot`'s (★). It never starts an analysis: a clip with nothing cached shows "Not
  analyzed — Clip ▸ Follow Subject… analyzes it". It is never persisted, so a proof that turns it
  on moves no defaults key.
- **VR-14 — `-RCDevAnalysisHold <s>` (dev tools only)** holds each analysis job for that many
  seconds before it lands, as `-RCDevSyncHold` holds Synchronize Audio's, so a proof can call a
  tool while a pass runs and see its answer past CJ-25's bound. It lives in `AnalysisLane.swift`
  (CJ2a's file) and is listed in root `CLAUDE.md`'s dev defaults.

**VR2a and VR2b — the planner, `reframe_clip` and Follow Subject.**

- **VR-20 — `reframe_clip {clip, follow, zoom?, where_empty?, replace?, from_width?, from_height?,
  backdrop?, subjects?}` frames one clip on the current canvas.**
  - `follow` is `subject` (faces, then people, then salient), `face`, `person`, `salient`,
    `center`, `fit` or `keep`. `center` is the window at fill × `zoom`, centred, with no moves.
    `fit` is the whole picture inside the canvas (the Fit placement) for the whole clip. `keep` is
    set_canvas's rescale rule, composed into the action ends as well (VR2b).
  - `where_empty` is `fit` (the default) or `center`: what a followed clip shows while there is
    nothing to follow (VR-24). `fit` means the same thing in both arguments.
  - `zoom` is 1 to 4 times fill, refused outside.
  - `from_width`/`from_height` name the canvas the clip's placement and actions were authored
    for, and default to the current one.
  - `subjects` is `{samples: [{t, faces?: [box], people?: [box], salient?: [box]}], shots: [t]}`,
    with `t` in media source ticks and each box `{x, y, w, h, c, id?}` in CJ-22's frame (centre
    and size normalised 0…1, display orientation, origin top-left). The core turns boxes into
    (★)'s Q frame through the media's displayed size, so a crop never invalidates the cache.
  - **Source time to clip time is one helper.** `clip_time_of_source(clip, media, t, round)`, in a
    new `core/src/clip_source_time.rs`, is `speech_in_clip`'s mapping lifted out whole: reflect
    over `media.duration` when the clip is reversed, subtract `in`, then `SpeedMap::time_at` when
    the clip is ramped, else divide by the base speed. `audio_duck_speech.rs` calls it in place of
    its closure, so the core has one implementation. Samples outside the played window are
    dropped.
- **VR-21 — Choosing the subject.** Tracks are CJ-31's linked face ids and VR-11's linked person
  ids, each split at every `shots` cut whether or not its ids restarted there. The primary track
  has the highest presence × median area × centrality. Faces outrank people. A person track that
  contains a face track (the face's centre inside the person box in at least 80 % of their shared
  samples) is that face's body and yields to it. Salient boxes are used only where no face or
  person is present. A rival track replaces the primary only after it scores 25 % higher for 2 s.
- **VR-22 — Composition.** The subject's face centre sits on the window's vertical centre line. In a
  window taller than wide it sits 38 % of the window's height from the top; otherwise it is
  centred. With no face, the top of the person box sits 12 % from the window's top. These are first
  numbers, set by VR-S2.
- **VR-23 — Moves.** The subject point is median-filtered over 1 s. The window moves only when the
  point leaves a dead zone (±10 % of the window width, ±8 % of its height). A move eases in and out
  for max(0.4 s, distance ÷ 0.5 window widths per second). No move starts within 0.5 s of the last
  one's end unless the subject would leave the window. A still subject makes no move. These are
  first numbers, set by VR-S2.
- **VR-24 — Cuts, loss and two people.**
  - **A shot change is a hard cut in the framing.** It is a one-frame linear action ending exactly
    on the cut's first frame. The new shot's first framing is placed on its subject's median over
    its first second, which the planner can see because it plans a whole clip.
  - **A lost subject is held for 1 s.** After that the planner moves to another track if there is
    one, else eases over 0.8 s to the `where_empty` treatment. It comes back once a subject has
    been seen for 0.6 s.
  - **Two people are framed together when they fit.** When both primary boxes, each widened by
    15 %, fit the window at the chosen zoom, the subject point is their union's. Otherwise the
    planner frames the primary under VR-21's hysteresis.
- **VR-25 — `backdrop`: the blurred copy goes on a named track.** When the framing shows the clip
  `fit` anywhere, the op adds one blurred copy, built by `add_blurred_background`'s own builder
  (which becomes `pub(crate)`), on the `backdrop` track. When that span is not free there, the op
  inserts a new back-most track itself and puts the copy there, as `add_blurred_background` does
  (`edit_background.rs` :12). Without `backdrop`, no copy is made and VR-7's first exception
  applies. `add_blurred_background` itself is unchanged.
- **VR-26 — What `reframe_clip` refuses**, each in its own sentence.
  - `follow` other than `keep` on a text, shape, graphic or adjustment clip.
  - A clip with no picture.
  - A nest clip with `subject`, `face`, `person` or `salient`. `center`, `fit` and `keep` are
    allowed, but `fit` with `backdrop` on a nest is refused in `add_blurred_background`'s own
    sentence (a nest's blurred copy would come out sharp).
  - A clip on a matte track, or one a matte cuts, unless `follow` is `keep`.
  - A clip whose base or action rotation is not 0, or whose motion has a `spin` slot, unless
    `follow` is `keep`.
  - `subject`, `face`, `person` or `salient` with no samples in the clip's window ("clip 12 has
    no subjects to follow; analyze it first").
  - Samples: more than 100,000; more than 8 boxes of a kind in one sample; times not strictly
    increasing; a coordinate outside 0…1 or a size of 0 or less.
  - **Until VR2b lands:** a clip carrying any action, unless `follow` is `keep` and the clip has
    no action naming x, y or scale ("clip 12 carries actions, which framing cannot compose with in
    this build"). VR2b removes this bullet.
  - A result equal to the clip is an identity.
- **VR-27 — Compose, or replace (VR2b).**
  - **Compose, the default.** The framing path F (scale and offset from the source canvas to this
    one) is composed into the clip's base and into the x, y and scale of every action end. Framing
    holds over an existing action are exact, because F is affine in (x, y, scale) and commutes with
    the lerp. The planner schedules its own moves in the gaps between existing actions. A move that
    cannot fit in a gap is carried by the action it overlaps, approximated by that action's curve,
    and still covering by VR-7.
  - **A cut inside an existing action A splits A around the cut's one-frame action,** as `split`
    narrows a straddled action (`edit_split.rs`'s `state_patch` and `narrow_to`, made
    `pub(crate)`): each head ends at the full evaluated state at its end over every key A names,
    not only x, y and scale, composed with the framing there; the tail keeps A's end and curve.
    For a linear A the split plays unchanged, volume included. For an eased A both halves carry
    A's curve, so the values at the split points and at A's end are kept and the shape between is
    re-eased on each side, which changes the picture and the sound between them; each such action
    is counted. An action that names `speed`, or one a trim left running past the clip's end
    (`add_action` would refuse its tail, AU-83's case), is not split: the cut is carried
    approximately by A's curve and counted.
  - **`replace: true`.** Every x, y and scale key is removed from the clip's action ends first, and
    an action left empty is removed. The base becomes the source canvas's Fit placement, and then F
    is composed. Clip ▸ Follow Subject replaces; Make Vertical Version composes.
  - **What the op tells the caller.** The op answers only applied, identity or refused (§5.5), so
    the counts (re-eased, carried approximately, motion spans) are recomputed by the command from
    the two handles, as the step's summary (VR-35) is.
- **VR-28 — The tool fills the subjects and answers within a bound.** `reframe_clip`'s tool does not
  publish `subjects` (`filledByTheApp`): the handler asks VR-12's kinds for the clip's window and
  waits for them up to CJ-25's bound. Past the bound it makes no edit and answers `{"analyzing":
  {"media": [ids], "covered": fraction}}` with the sentence "Still analyzing the media of clip 12
  (40 %); call reframe_clip again to apply." Its want stays held by the document until the job
  lands, fails, or the document closes, so the same call later applies from the cache. An agent
  that wants a hand-made path writes actions.
- **VR-29 — Clip ▸ Follow Subject… (VR2b)** applies `reframe_clip` with `replace: true` to each
  selected clip that has a picture, as one undo step "Follow Subject", in VR-34's order: an
  `add_track` "Backgrounds" at index 0 applied first (a refusal stops the command with its
  sentence), each `reframe_clip` with that track as `backdrop`, and a `remove_track` of it when no
  backdrop was needed. While the analysis runs it shows CJ-27's Analyzing sheet. The sheet has
  Follow (Subject, Faces, People, Salient Region, Center), Zoom (100–400 %; the default is 100 %
  when the canvas's shape differs from the picture's and 125 % when it matches, because at 100 % a
  same-shape picture has no room to move) and Where Empty (Show Whole, which is `fit`, and
  Center). The sheet remembers Follow and Where Empty (`FrameJobFollow*` keys); the tool reads no
  `UserDefaults` (AU-68 (f)'s rule). A dev default `-RCDevFollowAccept YES` presses its Follow
  button, the Match Audio precedent (AU-128).

**VR3 — Make Vertical Version.**

- **VR-30 — Make Vertical is one grouped edit applied to a document; the menu applies it to a
  copy.** `VerticalVersion.apply(to:shape:…)` is the step that FC's Make Short calls on its own
  document (FC-90). File ▸ Make Vertical Version… makes its copy with CJ5's derived-document
  builder (`ProjectDocument+Derived.swift`, CJ-51), handed the source's own handle unchanged — no
  `keep_range`, so every media stays — which copies the graphics and every media's caches,
  analysis included, under CJ-51's rules. The step is applied there. The source document never
  changes and gains no undo step. "Make a copy" is a checkbox, ticked by default and never
  remembered.
- **VR-31 — The copy opens with the step as its one undo step**, "Make Vertical" (FC-90's name, so
  both doors make the same step), and Undo in the copy shows the 16:9 project. The copy is
  untitled, named "<source name> (9:16)" or "(1:1)" until saved.
- **VR-32 — Shapes and sizes.** 9:16 and 1:1, keeping the source canvas's short side and even: from
  1920 × 1080 they are 1080 × 1920 and 1080 × 1080. A shape equal to the current canvas is not
  offered. 4:5 is asked at VR3.
- **VR-33 — How each top-level clip is treated, in this order (the first class that matches).**
  1. **An existing blurred backdrop** (named "Blurred Background", behind a clip with the same
     source, in point, start and duration): deleted when that clip is followed or shown `fit` in
     this run (it would never show, or the run's own backdrop replaces it); otherwise re-filled
     at the new canvas's fill scale, centred (`set_video {x: 0, y: 0, scale}`).
  2. **A plate**: a shape rectangle the old canvas's size at x = y = 0 and scale 1, named
     "Background" or not, gets `set_shape` to the new canvas's size; an image or still named
     "Background" at the old canvas's fill scale, centred, gets `set_video` at the new fill
     scale, centred.
  3. **A full-frame picture**: a media, still or image clip whose rect at its first frame spans
     one whole axis of the old canvas (within 1 px) and is centred within 2 % on the other is
     followed with `subject`. A pillarboxed 4:3 or a letterboxed scope picture counts. A
     rotated, `spin`-moving or matte clip is `keep` instead, and listed. A clip with another
     motion is followed, and listed with VR-7's motion exception.
  4. **A full-frame nest clip** is `center` (a nest is a 16:9 picture; nothing inside it changes).
  5. **A graphic the old canvas's size** is VR4's (VR-42).
  6. **Every other visual clip** is `keep`: a camera bubble, a picture-in-picture, a title, a
     shape, a non-full graphic.
- **VR-34 — The order of the step, and where it stops.**
  1. `set_canvas {width, height}` with no rescale.
  2. `add_track` at index 0, named "Backgrounds".

     Steps 1 and 2 are applied to a pure handle first. A refusal of either stops the step with its
     sentence and nothing made, because the grouped edit's fold runs on after a refusal.
  3. VR-33's classes 1 and 2 (backdrops and plates).
  4. `reframe_clip` per class-3, class-4 and class-6 clip, with `from_width`/`from_height` the old
     canvas and `backdrop` that track, each tried in turn on the handle. A refused one is tried
     again as `keep` and listed with the core's sentence; a refused `keep` stops the step with
     nothing made.
  5. `remove_track {track}` on that track, when no backdrop was needed. `remove_empty_tracks` takes
     no track and would also remove the person's own empty tracks.
  6. VR4's captions and graphics.

  The list that passed is then applied as one grouped edit, which reproduces the handle (the same
  ops on the same handle mint the same ids: `CaptionLayout.place`'s probe precedent).
- **VR-35 — The summary.** The sheet's result lists clips followed, shown whole, kept, re-filled,
  removed and not followed, each with its reason ("a nest", "rotated", "on a matte track", "moves
  by its own motion: Drift"), and the counts of actions re-eased and moves carried approximately
  (VR-27). `make_vertical_version` answers the same lists.
- **VR-36 — `make_vertical_version {shape, follow?, zoom?, where_empty?, captions?, copy?, path?}`**
  mirrors the sheet. It runs off main and never asks the person anything. With `copy` (the default)
  it opens the copy, saved at `path` when given, as `new_project` does. With `copy: false` it
  applies the step to the addressed project. It waits for analysis up to CJ-25's bound and past it
  answers as VR-28 does, opening nothing. It is ask-first for the assistant when it names `path`,
  AI-7's own reason (a file written where the model chose), amending AI-7 by one row as FC-83 does
  for `make_short`.
- **VR-37 — Analysis comes before the copy, in the source's cache,** so the copy's cache holds
  copies of the source's analysis files (CJ-51), and a later run on the source reuses them. Stop
  on the Analyzing sheet makes nothing.
- **VR-38 — The owner's verdict on vertical versions** (JOB-35), recorded after the trial as GR-9
  was. It says whether the framing, the whole-shot treatment and the captions were what the owner
  would post, and whether re-making copies after master edits was a cost (VR7a's question).

### Spikes

Each rule is fixed before its run and stored by SHA-256 (CJ-7). Its record goes in the road map.

- **VR-S1 — People and saliency on video** (at VR1's start, after CJ-S2's verdict, on CJ-32's pinned
  device).
  - *Question:* at what rate and frame size do `VNDetectHumanRectanglesRequest` r2 and
    `VNGenerateAttentionBasedSaliencyImageRequest` r2 run deterministically and fast enough, and
    do person boxes hold when the face is lost?
  - *Instrument:* `tools/proof/creator_spike/vr_subjects/` (synchronous VN* calls, as
    `effects_spike/vision_job.swift`), reading frames through CJ-23's reader. Inputs: S-TH1 (with
    its leave, turn-away and side-on beats marked by the owner), S-VR1 (HLG), and CJ's
    moving-still fixture.
  - *Rules:*
    1. **The rate** is `faces`' rate if both requests together, at `faces`' frame size, run at
       ≥ 4× realtime (CJ-S2's bar); otherwise every other `faces` sample.
    2. **The frame size** is `faces`' unless person recall there is more than 1 percentage point
       under recall at a long side of 1440 on S-TH1, in which case it is 1440.
    3. **Determinism:** three runs on the pinned device give byte-identical files. Otherwise STOP:
       the kind's stamp carries a tolerance instead (an amendment before VR1's code, CJ-S2's form).
    4. **People stay** if the person box is found in ≥ 90 % of S-TH1's turned-away and side-on
       samples. Otherwise `people` is dropped from `subjects` and VR-21's person tier is removed
       by amendment before VR1's code.
    5. **HLG:** with S-VR1, person recall through CJ-23's converted path is recorded; no rule
       (CJ-23 decides the path).
- **VR-S2 — The planner's first numbers** (with VR2a, over cached analyses, no video).
  - *Question:* which dead zone, pan speed and composition give a talking head that is framed
    without fidget?
  - *Instrument:* the core's planner run from a test binary over S-TH1's cached `faces` and
    `subjects`, T1's and T2's, and the canned fixtures. The grid is dead zone {6, 10, 15} % ×
    speed {0.3, 0.5, 0.8} windows/s × headroom {33, 38, 42} %. It measures containment (the face
    centre inside the window's central 60 %) and moves per minute.
  - *Rule:* the setting with the highest containment at no more than 6 moves per minute. If no
    setting reaches 97 % containment, the dead zone shrinks one step and the cap rises to 8.
    JOB-31 judges the feel.
- **VR-S3 — Face-to-mic agreement** (at VR6's start).
  - *Question:* does mouth opening against SW-21's turns tell which face is which mic?
  - *Instrument:* over S-PC2 recorded with a microphone each (and the two-face moving-still with
    synthetic turns), the agreement for the true pairing and for the swapped one.
  - *Rule:* the threshold is the midpoint between the lowest true-pair agreement and the highest
    swapped-pair agreement when they separate. If they do not, VR6 always asks (VR-61), and the
    guide says so.
- **VR-S4 — A framing switch in the preview** (before VR7a's code, only if the owner says yes).
  - *Question:* how long does the preview take to rebuild when the canvas size changes on a
    300-clip project (measured with `set_canvas` toggling today), and does a per-framing plan fit
    the decoder budget?
  - *Rule:* if a rebuild is under 1 s on the owner's Mac, the preview rebuilds on switch. If not,
    it keeps the last two framings' compositions. A framing whose plan warns past 8 decoders is
    named in the export sheet, as today.

  20 s; the face leaving for 2 s and returning; two faces 400 px apart then 1400 px apart; a still
  face; a `shots` list with cuts at known frames; a screen card with no subject. VR2a, VR2b, VR3,
  VR4 and VR6 run on these, byte-exact on any Mac.
- Vision's tolerance rows stay in CJ3 (faces) and VR1 (people and saliency). A planner proof
  never runs Vision.

### Risks

- **Upscaled 1080p.** A 1080p source fills a 1080 × 1920 frame at ×1.78, which is visibly soft.
  Nothing hides it. The guide says to shoot 4K for vertical, and JOB-33 judges it.
- **Vision on log, dark or small faces.** CJ-S2 measures faces on the owner's footage, and VR-S1
  people; a person too small at the chosen size forces 1440, at analysis cost.
- **Results that move with macOS.** A new OS can change Vision's answers. CJ-22's stamp pins the
  kind's version, the OS build and the device, so a new OS re-analyses on the next command. Proofs
  compare against the cache, not against a recomputation.
- **The wrong subject.** A poster on the wall, a face on a monitor, or an audience member can win
  VR-21's score. The hysteresis, the nudge and the Follow popup are the answers. A recording with a
  sidecar never follows faces (VR-51).
- **Composition inside existing actions.** A framing move inside an existing action is
  approximated by that action's curve, and splitting an eased action re-eases both halves. Both
  are counted in the summary. Coverage still holds (VR-7).
- **Motion presets.** A clip with a moving `video.motion` keeps it, and the coverage guarantee
  excludes its span; a During motion excludes the whole clip. The summary names each.
- **Timeline clutter.** A long take gets many framing actions on its lane. Each is an ordinary
  action the person can delete.
- **Decoder budget.** Each `fit` clip adds a blurred copy that decodes the same file. The plan
  warns past 8 concurrent video tracks, and it does not refuse.
- **Track cap.** Backdrops share one track (VR-25). Only overlapping `fit` clips on different
  tracks need a second. At 64 the step is refused in the core's sentence, nothing is made, and the
  summary names it.
- **Graphics written by people or agents.** A graphic that does not lay itself out from
  `ctx.width` and `ctx.height` may overflow the tall frame. Only the bundled templates and their
  unedited copies are fixed (VR-43, VR-44). The guide and `docs/graphics-api.md` say how.
- **Portrait projects change.** VR-41 changes Subtitles and Text ▸ Presets on every portrait
  project, not only vertical versions; landscape and square output is byte-identical.
- **Untimed or restyled captions** cannot be re-paged. Their track is kept, placed by `keep`, and
  listed.
- **Analysis time.** A one-hour recording takes minutes even windowed, and three kinds read it.
  The Analyzing sheet has Stop, a tool answers `analyzing` past CJ-25's bound instead of blocking,
  and the cache makes a second run free.
- **The copy drifts from the master.** That is by design until linked versions exist. JOB-35 says
  whether it matters.
- **Files at the cap.** `edit_action.rs` (595) must take nothing: if VR2b needs a helper there, it
  pays the end-patch toll first. `CaptionLayout.swift` (581) pays its toll at VR4.
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift` and `ReelCore.swift` pay theirs at VR7a and VR7b.
- **Linked versions are large.** VR7a–VR9 touch every op that carries actions and the
  recipe-and-plan seam. The owner's yes at VR7a is the gate, and VR-S4 runs before the code.

### Not in this bet

- Stacked, side-by-side and corner-bubble layouts, and moving the recorded camera (bet 6). VR uses
  them once they exist.
- Switching between camera angles by speaker (bet 5). VR6 frames one wide shot only.
- Masks, cutouts or any per-pixel subject work. Framing uses boxes alone.
- Following clips inside a nest, matte pairs, or rotated clips. They are kept and listed.
- A language model or cloud model choosing the framing, and Apple FoundationModels.
- Motion blur on pans, stabilisation and optical-flow retiming. These are lifted non-goals, not
  scheduled here.
- Platform safe-zone overlays and named platform export rows (the next tier's publish slice).
- A range of the timeline as a vertical version. That is CJ5's New Project from Range or FC's
  Make Short, followed by this step.
- A File ▸ Duplicate command. The copy is CJ-51's derived document.
- Keyframes. Framing is actions, per §2's idea 3.
